title: Introduce weighted shadow traffic and region-tier fallback policy for safe model rollouts
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: implement a safe, configurable routing and fallback layer that enables weighted shadow traffic, per-region tier-aware failover, and automated rollback triggers during model variant rollouts. This ticket designs and implements the policy engine, compatibility validations, and the runtime hooks to enforce tier thresholds and cross-region fallbacks. Motivation: previous deployments exposed edge cases where model variants with incompatible KV cache layouts or quantization semantics caused elevated tail latency or output regressions. We need a rollout system that can run canaries, A/B tests, and shadow traffic in parallel while guaranteeing graceful degradation and a clear auto-rollback surface for production incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine supports weighted shadow routes (0-100%) per route and per-region
Model manifest includes compatibility signature; deployment blocked if major incompatibility detected
Tier-aware failover: if primary region capacity below configured threshold, traffic seamlessly falls back to next tier/region with no more than X% request loss
Auto-rollback triggers: P95 latency degradation >30% or error rate >0.5% for 5 consecutive minutes or quality regression on eval set >2%
End-to-end tests and chaos tests validate fallback without request duplication or KV cache corruption
New metrics exported: canary_latency_ratio, shadow_error_rate, fallback_events (region->region mapping)
design_decisions: Use a weighted shadow approach rather than full duplication for early validation to reduce cost and avoid double billing semantics
Introduce a small immutable compatibility signature in model manifests (architecture, kv-schema-version, quantization-profile) to gate rollouts
Prefer tier-aware routing over naive round-robin to preserve SLAs for paid customers in higher tiers
Implement deterministic sticky routing for sessions to avoid cache thrashing during canaries unless explicitly disabled
Auto-rollback handled by a controller that consumes streaming metrics and writes rollbacks to the deployment API; decisions are logged and auditable
implementation_notes: Add compatibility validation in admission controller (deploy-time) and in runtime router (runtime check for mismatched manifests)
Extend envoy-like routing table with weight/shadow boolean and fallback mapping to region-tier vector
Expose a new field in rollout config: fallback_tiers: [{region: us-west-2, min_capacity_pct: 40}, ...]
KV cache hotkey handling: ensure shadow traffic never writes back to shared caches; use isolated shadow cache namespaces
Performance: optimized path for 0% shadow weight to avoid any runtime overhead
Backpressure: when fallback triggers, route degrade path should prefer read-only variants if available to preserve consistency
test_plan: Unit tests for policy engine (weights, shadow routing, fallback mapping)
Integration test that deploys two model variants: canary and stable; asserts metrics flow and rollback on induced latency spike
Chaos test to simulate regional outage and validate tier failover with <1% 5xx spike
Compatibility fuzz tests to detect subtle kv-schema mismatches that previously caused cache corruption
Synthetic eval job to run a deterministic prompt set against shadowed responses and compute quality delta
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Pilot: 0->1% weighted shadow in us-west-2 for 2 hours; collect latency, error, and eval metrics
Phase 2 - Canary: 5% live canary traffic in us-west-2 with rollback policy enabled; monitor for 24 hours
Phase 3 - Regional ramp: if metrics stable, increase to 25% and enable tier-aware routing to us-east-1 as backup
Phase 4 - Gradual global rollout: expand weights per region with automated gating and human-in-the-loop for production-severe regressions
Rollback semantics: controller performs automatic rollback and notifies on-call + creates a rollback incident with list of impacted routes
